tweet.text:
Here is a shorter version of my city poster prompt. It works quite well. 

🟣  PromptShare GPT 2.6: 2x2 grid, 16:9, do this for 4 famous ciites: 
INPUT = [SUBJECT]

V = {
  WORD      : shortest recognizable name,
  CONTENT   : auto | history | culture | geography | science | concept,
  WORLD     : auto | architecture | landscape | machinery | ecosystem | diorama,
  DEPTH     : layered 3D | architectural cutaway | miniature collage,
  DENSITY   : high detail, controlled hierarchy,
  TIMELINE  : 3–6 verified milestones | conceptual sequence,
  OVERLAY   : technical atlas | drafting | cartographic,
  LAYOUT    : auto | panoramic | stacked | wordscape | 2×2 series,
  ACCENT    : one subject-derived meaningful color,
  FORMAT    : auto | portrait | landscape | square
}

C₁  SEMANTIC + HISTORICAL DNA (master)
    research/infer SUBJECT identity, canonical name, landmarks, events, people, artifacts, geography, symbols and chronology; rank by recognition × significance × visual potential. Select only factual, subject-specific content.
    ¬C₁ = invented history / generic landmarks / arbitrary symbolism.

C₂  MONUMENTAL TYPOGRAPHIC ARCHITECTURE
    construct WORD in gigantic ultra-black condensed grotesk, tight optical spacing; transform glyphs into physical architectural volumes, not image masks. Strokes → structural walls, counters → cavities, spacing → environments, baseline → continuous terrain. Preserve instant word recognition.
    ¬C₂ = flat photo-filled fonts / distorted lettering / ordinary text beside illustrations.

C₃  ADAPTIVE LETTER-WORLD ENGINE
    populate glyph interiors with ranked SUBJECT elements: miniature landmarks, events, figures, artifacts, landscapes or mechanisms. Match content to glyph geometry; allow structures to rise, intersect counters, bridge letters and extend into foreground. Adapt [WORLD] × [DEPTH] to subject identity.
    ¬C₃ = random stock scenery / generic city skylines / disconnected miniatures / inconsistent scale.

C₄  MULTISCALE NARRATIVE HIERARCHY
    engineer three reading distances: FAR → unmistakable monumental WORD; MID → recognizable historical/conceptual panorama; CLOSE → intricate meaningful micro-scenes. Prioritize word silhouette → iconic structures → supporting elements → tiny figures → annotations.
    ¬C₄ = uniform visual weight / illegible word / meaningless detail density.

C₅  TECHNICAL ATLAS INTELLIGENCE
    surround typography with restrained [OVERLAY]: hairline dimensions, axes, grids, arrows, accurate geographic coordinates, construction callouts and subtle registration marks. Annotate only real spatial, structural or historical relationships; lines ≈0.5–1.5px, pale gray.
    ¬C₅ = fake engineering data / unrelated labels / decorative grids / annotation clutter.

C₆  CHRONOLOGY + CONCEPTUAL SEQUENCING
    integrate [TIMELINE] along the baseline: verified dates, defining events and concise labels; for timeless/abstract subjects substitute ordered mechanisms, stages or components. Connect milestones to corresponding letter-world scenes.
    ¬C₆ = fabricated dates / generic placeholder events / disconnected chronology.

C₇  SUBJECT-RESPONSIVE TOPOLOGY
    infer [LAYOUT]: comparable subjects → balanced 2×2 atlas; long WORD → panoramic; vertical identity → stacked monument; iconic place → continuous architectural wordscape; process → evolving glyph environments; otherwise centered semantic micro-world. Maintain consistent grid and generous breathing room.
    ¬C₇ = fixed layout / repetitive skylines / cropped letters / crowded composition.

C₈  SWISS MUSEUM–COLLAGE LANGUAGE
    monumental Swiss typography × historical architectural collage × technical drafting × photographic museum atlas. Warm-white paper, charcoal-black type, mostly monochrome realistic miniatures, ONE [ACCENT] for meaningful identity. Neutral editorial light, subtle grain, crisp hairlines.
    ¬C₈ = colorful infographic clutter / cartoon rendering / glossy effects / excessive boxes.

η   ARCHITECTURAL + HISTORICAL COHERENCE
    seamless letter–world integration, believable miniature depth, accurate subject-specific scenes, monumental readability, layered photographic realism, disciplined scale, precise technical labels, museum-grade editorial finish.

FORBIDDEN = generic skylines · photo-clipped fonts · invented milestones · arbitrary landmarks · fake dimensions · unrelated annotations · flat typography · inconsistent perspective · decorative clutter · weak subject recognition
